front: Passing score on every Claude certification exam
back: 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000

front: Time limit on every Claude certification exam
back: 120 minutes, with about 135 minutes of total seat time

front: How long is a Claude credential valid
back: 12 months from the date you earn it

front: What does on-time renewal involve
back: A free, open-book, non-proctored assessment on Anthropic Partner Academy, retakable as often as needed

front: What happens if a credential lapses
back: You must pass the full exam again at full fee

front: Retake waiting periods after failed attempts
back: 14 days after the first, 30 after the second, 90 after the third

front: Maximum attempts per exam per rolling 12 months
back: Four

front: Free cancellation or reschedule window
back: At least 24 hours before the appointment; inside that, the fee is forfeited

front: Who delivers the exams
back: Pearson VUE, online proctored through OnVUE or at a test center

front: Where does the digital badge come from
back: Credly, by email after a pass

front: Which exam does not count toward partner tier eligibility
back: Claude Certified Associate

front: Partner tier discounts on exam fees
back: Select, Preferred, and Global Premier partners receive 50% off, applied at checkout

front: How is the exam scored, in one phrase
back: Criterion-referenced: against a fixed standard, not against other candidates

front: What does the score report show beyond pass or fail
back: The scaled score and percent-correct per domain

front: Is there an official practice exam
back: No. The previous platform's was retired in the Pearson migration; the exam guides' sample questions are the only official items

front: What is the authoritative scope of an exam
back: The blueprint in its official exam guide; anything outside it is not tested

front: Are the exams open book
back: No. No notes, documentation, translation tools, or AI assistants

front: Who may currently sit these exams
back: People at Claude Partner Network organizations, registering with a recognized company email

front: How long do partner email domain record changes take
back: 7 to 10 days, so resolve them before you plan to sit

front: What does the exam NDA cover
back: Questions, answer options, and scenarios, explicitly including study groups and online forums

front: Where can you take the official courses without a partner account
back: The public Claude Academy; every course is free there

front: Glossary: Blueprint
back: The exam content outline in each exam guide: the domains measured, their weights, and the objectives items are written against. The authoritative scope of the exam

front: Glossary: Domain weight
back: The approximate share of scored items drawn from a domain, for example 33.1% for the Developer exam's Applications and integration domain

front: Glossary: Task statement
back: A numbered capability within a domain, used in the Architect Foundations guide, that items are written against

front: Glossary: MQC
back: Minimally qualified candidate: the profile of the weakest examinee who should still pass, which the passing standard is calibrated to

front: Glossary: Criterion-referenced
back: Scored against a fixed standard rather than against other candidates. There is no curve

front: Glossary: Scaled score
back: The reported score on a 100 to 1,000 range, equated so results are comparable across exam forms of slightly different difficulty

front: Glossary: Cut score
back: The passing threshold: 720 scaled, for all four exams

front: Glossary: Item
back: An exam question. Multiple-choice items have one best answer; multiple-response items state how many responses to select

front: Glossary: Scenario-based exam
back: The Architect Foundations format: 4 scenarios drawn from a published bank of 6, each framing a set of items

front: Glossary: Exam form
back: A specific assembled version of an exam; forms vary slightly, which scaled scoring corrects for

front: Glossary: NDA
back: The non-disclosure agreement accepted before the exam starts: exam content may not be shared, reproduced, or discussed, including in study groups and forums

front: Glossary: Pearson VUE
back: The company that delivers the exams, online and at test centers, since June 30, 2026

front: Glossary: OnVUE
back: Pearson's online proctoring application, run on your own computer under remote supervision

front: Glossary: Test center
back: A physical Pearson location with provided equipment, the alternative to online proctoring

front: Glossary: Credly
back: The digital badging platform that issues the shareable credential after a pass

front: Glossary: CPN
back: The Claude Partner Network, whose member organizations are eligible for certification

front: Glossary: Partner tier
back: An organization's CPN level: Registered pays list price; Select, Preferred, and Global Premier receive 50% off exams

front: Glossary: Prep path
back: The curated course sequence on Partner Academy for a specific certification

front: Glossary: Exam guide
back: The official PDF for each certification: blueprint, sample questions, policies, and scoring. The single most important study document

front: Glossary: Renewal assessment
back: The free, open-book, non-proctored assessment on Partner Academy that extends a credential 12 months when passed before expiry

front: Glossary: Lapse
back: Letting a credential expire without renewing; regaining it requires the full exam at full fee

front: Glossary: Appeal
back: A formal challenge to a certification decision or result, filed with Pearson within 14 days

front: Glossary: Question report
back: Flagging a possibly faulty item to Pearson; separate from an appeal and never counted against you

front: Glossary: Accommodations
back: Testing adjustments for documented needs, requested through Pearson and approved before scheduling
